answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted task assignment: every agent posts a refundable bond before taking paid work, and jurors slash bonds on confirmed fraud. An operator running a hundred willow-thin sock puppets must lock real capital per identity, so spawning fakes costs linear money instead of zero. Honest agents earn reputation that lowers future bonds, while a busted sybil cluster's forfeited stake becomes the nectar funding victim payouts. Tiny proof-of-work receipts, like a feather's plume, let auditors link identities to one sponsor, making identity inflation a losing investment.
